questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Sarah / will singing / at the concert / on Saturday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. will singing .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is intended to describe a future action.
 
• In the future continuous tense, the correct structure is **"will be + present participle (verb+ing)".**
 
• The segment **"will singing"** is incorrect because "**will**" needs to be followed by "be" to form the correct future continuous tense.
 
• The correct form should be "will be singing". Therefore, the segment "will singing" contains the grammatical error.

Correct sentence: *Sarah will be singing at the concert on Saturday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Continuous Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + will be + verb (base form + ing)
 
• **Example:** They will be traveling to Europe next month.
 
• **Usage:** Describes an ongoing action that will happen in the future.
 
 
 
• **Present Participle (verb+ing):** The form of the verb used to indicate continuous action.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Guard over / making mistakes / by carefully checking / the assigned task.
questions.solution:
```html

The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The phrase "Guard over" is not idiomatic in this context.

• The correct idiomatic expression should be "Guard against" when referring to preventing mistakes.

• The rest of the sentence segments are grammatically correct and logically consistent.

• Therefore, the segment "Guard over" should be corrected to "Guard against" to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Correct sentence: *Guard against making mistakes by carefully checking the assigned task*.

• **Option 4: "making mistakes"** - This phrase correctly identifies the action to be guarded against and is grammatically correct.

questions.question:
The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

This is the eldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India.

options.text: This is the more older standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the most old standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the more elder standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the oldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'This is the oldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the superlative form of the adjective 'oldest' should be used instead of 'eldest'.
 
• The word **'eldest'** is typically used for people, especially in the context of family relationships, while **'oldest'** is used for objects, structures, and other non-living things.
 
• Therefore, the correct form is 'oldest'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *This is the oldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When discussing age or duration in the context of objects or structures, use **'oldest'** to indicate the greatest age.
 
• The word **'eldest'** is reserved for the oldest person among a group of people, typically within a family.
 
 
• **Example (correct usage of 'eldest'):** *She is the eldest of the three siblings.*
 
• **Example (correct usage of 'oldest'):** *This is the oldest tree in the park.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

I regret / in notify that / the model you want/ is out of stock.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**in notify**" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct expression should be "**to notify**" as the verb "regret" is followed by an infinitive ("to" + base verb) when expressing formal notification or announcements.
 
• Thus, the corrected sentence should be: "*I regret to notify that the model you want is out of stock.*"
 
• Therefore, the grammatical error lies in **segment 2**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I regret **to notify** that the model you want is out of stock."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Use "**regret to + verb**" when expressing formal regret about an action you're doing now or about to do (e.g., regret to inform, regret to announce).
 
• Use "**regret + verb-ing**" when expressing sorrow about a past action (e.g., I regret saying that).

**Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

questions.solution: The correct answer is** 'warn him'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. • Here,** 'warned him' **should be used instead of **'warn him'.** • The given sentence is in the **past tense.** • Hence the use of simple present tense here is grammatically incorrect. • Hence, '**warn**' should be changed into '**warned**'. **Correct Sentence:__** *He stopped copying when the examiner **warned him.***** ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है। • यहां** 'warn him' **के बजाय **'warned him' **का इस्तेमाल किया जाना चाहिए। • दिया गया वाक्य **past tense **में है। • अतः यहाँ** simple present tense** का प्रयोग व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है। • इसलिए '**warn**' को '**warned**' में बदल देना चाहिए। 30:T939, The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**
